messages:
Ops-Lead: Heads up — after pushing the new VPC egress guardrail this morning we're seeing GPU warm-pool nodes in eu-west1 fail to finish warm-up. Keystore reports and KMS throttles in the logs. Anyone on call?

Jonah: I'm seeing a spike of decrypt errors: "decrypt_error: KMS Throttling" on warm pool nodes. NAT gateway QPS also shot up.

Maya: https://redwood.ops/trace/abcd1234 shows the warmup timeline — long tail on first decrypts :eyes:

sre-bot: alert: warm-pool-scale-failure at 2026-03-20T09:12Z reason=keystore-decrypt-errors component=warm-pool

Security-Eng: We rolled the egress deny to force privatelink-only outbound. That might be blocking keystore -> AWS KMS endpoints. Which SG/rule id did we apply?

Ops-Lead: Rule id is sg-guard-2026-v2 in prod-eu. It allows privatelink endpoints only. Keystore still uses shared NAT for some bootstrap nodes — so they lost KMS access.

Amelia: Short-term mitigation: add an outbound exception for AWS KMS IPs on the node SG or create a KMS VPC endpoint. Which is faster for eu-west1?

Jonah: Privatelink KMS is available in eu-west1 but needs infra change. Quick rollback: add SG egress allow to 54.240.0.0/16 (example) or allow by prefix-list for KMS. For immediate fix, SG exception is fastest.

Maya: Logs also show lots of audit uploads failing: "put_object s3 audit 403" — looks like an IAM condition got stricter around the same time. Could be role boundary change on the keystore role.

Ops-Lead: Also seeing kms_request_latency climb to 2.5s. @Security-Eng — did we enable debug-level CloudTrail/audit for KMS? That could be increasing call volume.

Security-Eng: Yes — we enabled full audit for compliance verification for 48h (sample=100%) which caused additional metadata calls. Rolling it back to sample=10% now.

Amelia: If we reduce audit noise, warm-pool should recover, but the keystore still does many individual decrypts on startup. We should batch decrypts in the keystore agent (PR #4021). That will reduce KMS QPS.

Jonah: Proposed rollback plan: 1) temporary SG outbound exception to KMS prefix-list in prod-eu 2) revert audit debug from 100% -> 10% 3) deploy keystore decrypt batching (canary) 4) monitor warm-pool success and NAT egress cost. Agree?

Ops-Lead: Agreed. I'll open a canary for eu-west1 only. Amelia/Jonah — can you estimate cost delta if we allow outbound to KMS via NAT for warmup window? Need a quick number for finance/compliance.

Maya: Rough calc: extra NAT egress for warmup traffic ~350 USD/day for the eu warm-pool churn, assuming 10k concurrent decrypts and 200KB per request. It's cheaper than missing SLA but let's keep window short. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

sre-bot: action created: TICKET-4534 - temporary egress exception + audit rollback + deploy PR #4021. Assignees: Jonah, Amelia, Security-Eng.

Security-Eng: I'll coordinate with compliance and log the temporary exception window. Mark as high priority and tag for post-mortem. :lock:

Jonah: Quick SG snippet to add (replace with our prefix-list):
```
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-egress --group-id sg-abcdef01 --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 54.240.0.0/16 --description "temp allow KMS for keystore warmup"
```

Amelia: After canary success we'll revert SG and keep PR #4021 in canary for 24h, then promote. Also schedule a follow-up to review sampling policy for audit so we don't spike KMS again.

Ops-Lead: Thanks — will update incident channel and start the canary. Post-mortem checklist: root cause (egress policy + audit sampling) + fix (batching) + controls (monitor KMS QPS).

Maya: ping me when canary goes green, I'll run evals on latency and error rates.

sre-bot: incident status: mitigation_in_progress.

Ops-Lead: closing loop here — temporary fix in flight. Will post summary when done. :white_check_mark:
